linkedin.content:
Lexical ingestion is rarely just “put these rows in a database.” The difficult part is keeping every edit traceable when sources disagree in structure, orthography, gloss language, or completeness.

I built a small, project-owned proof around that boundary. It ingests one synthetic Toolbox-style source and one CSV lexicon into SQLite while preserving every raw field, source record ID, field locator, and source hash. English-gloss normalization is stored separately. Supplied IPA is copied, never invented. Invalid records go to a deterministic reject ledger. A replay makes zero writes, and an injected failure rolls the transaction back.

The sample is deliberately small and candid: it uses no customer data, no real Toolbox corpus, and no customer schema. It is workflow evidence, not a compatibility or linguistic-accuracy claim.

Code, database, report, and reproducible checks:
https://github.com/lachlanchen/LazyPromotion/tree/main/examples/lexical-ingest-proof

The related LexiconAtlas release shows the downstream read-only graph: terms, morphemes, historical forms, translations, relationships, and provenance kept as separate objects.
https://github.com/lachlanchen/LexiconAtlas/releases/latest
